speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing shortness of breath and increased abdominal girth alongside a large ovarian mass. To help narrow down the cause, are you currently experiencing any unintended weight loss or persistent nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rapid onset of symptoms and the large ovarian mass, I need to assess for associated fluid accumulation. Do you have any difficulty breathing when lying flat, and have you noticed swelling in your legs or ankles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

text: RESULTS: Pelvic_Ultrasound: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present. CA-125: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CA-125 and large ovarian mass with ascites, I need to rule out a benign condition like Meigs' syndrome. Do you have any history of heart disease or liver problems that might explain the fluid accumulation?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: To further evaluate the respiratory symptoms associated with the ascites, do you have any chest pain or a persistent cough? I will also request imaging to assess the lungs and pleural space. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-Ray: Right-sided pleural effusion. Abdominal_CT: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of an ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion with normal tumor markers strongly suggests Meigs' syndrome, likely due to an ovarian fibroma. I will now proceed to confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs' Syndrome
